architecture.mechanism: A 12V battery is kept charged by an auxiliary renewable harvester (photovoltaic cell plus kinetic energy harvester) with voltage-sensor monitoring and relay-based load management, ensuring a sustainable power supply and dynamic load management based on power availability and demand.
architecture.intervention: Install a low-wattage PV trickle charger (and/or a small kinetic/vibration harvester) on the vehicle's 12V starter battery, interposed by a charge controller with a voltage sensor and a relay that priority-switches or disconnects non-essential parasitic loads when the battery voltage falls below a threshold, so the battery is replenished and protected during idle periods without manual terminal disconnect.
architecture.expected_effect: The harvested trickle charge offsets the standing parasitic drain, holding the battery above the no-start threshold so full cranking power remains available after at least one week idle.
architecture.falsification_test: Baseline-test a vehicle battery's resting voltage and cold-cranking amps, then leave the vehicle idle for 7 days with the parasitic load active; repeat with the PV trickle-charge/relay controller fitted and log battery voltage every hour. The mechanism is falsified if the 7-day voltage under the intervention does not stay above ~12.4 V (or fails to deliver rated CCA and a start), or if the relay fails to shed the parasitic load when voltage drops below the set threshold.
